ANNUAL .COMMUNICATION OI' THE

Executive Council.

New York City.
To THE Fortieth Convention of the Psi Upsilon Fraternity :

The Executive Council would respectfully submit their annual communication.

It gives the Council much pleasure to
congratulate the Fraternity upon its
continued prosperity. With one exception all the Chapters report themselves in a

flourishing condition. The single exception is the Alpha, an account of whose
troubles will be found further on. There seems to have been a
slight falling off
in our numbers since last year, but that is almost entirely occasioned by the defec
tion of the Alpha. An exhibit of our active membership is given below.
The Council reports with much gratification the adoption of the two amend
ments to the Constitution passed at the last Convention. We believe that the
limitations as to membership are now as good as can be desired. We hope that

they will be more thoroughly observed in future than they have been during the
past year.
The Resolution of the last Convention directing the Council to print the Records
of the Convention was carefully executed, and we believe it has proved the wisdom
of the Convention. One great object gained was that the copies were all com
pared and found to agree with the official records. The expense was $37, being
a
saving of about $75 over the old way of distributing the records. We would
ask that the Recorder be instructed to forward the records as soon as
possible
after the Convention. We also call the attention of the Recorder to the fact that
the Convention rules require him to forward a copy of each general resolution
adopted by the Convention, and that the copy must be indorsed as correct by the
President of the Convention. Last year there was considerable delay owing to
the mistakes of the printer ; but next year we promise a great economy of time.
Y The Council have to report that the petition for a new Chapter at Cornell

University was refused, three Chapters voting against it. The petition for a new
Chapter at Syracuse University was also refused, two Chapters voting against it.
Through some misapprehension of a letter from a member of the Council to the
petitioners at Syracuse, the petitioners supposed that if the two Chapters voting
against them should change their votes the charter for a Chapter would be granted
to them. Accordingly, they brought such arguments to bear upon the Chapters
which voted against the petition that they (the two Chapters aforesaid) wrote to
the Council, asking that their votes should be changed. After mature deliber
ation, the Council unanimously decided that it had not the power to re-open the
question after the decision of the Fraternity had been promulgated. This
decision of the Council we deem to be not only warranted by the Constitution,
but a necessity for the proper protection of the Fraternity. The evil effects of

14

allowing a Chapter to change its vote upon question referred to it by the Con
a

vention is easily understood, as positive decision ever given.
there would be no
When informed that the Council would not reopen the question, the petitioners
sent in a new petition to the Council, asking the Council to lay it before the

Chapters for ratification. The Council, although believing that no Chapter should
be founded unless the arguments in its favor were very strong, decided that, as

apparently all the Chapters were in favor of the establishment of a new Chapter at
"Syracuse University, it was only just that the matter should be again laid before
them. This was done accordingly, and the petition was again refused, four Chap
ters voting against it and three in favor of it. The Council wish to call the
attention of the Convention to the fact that the Chapters do not send in the result
of their votes. It is seldom that over five or six Chapters inform the Council of
their wishes upon any question referred to them. In case a Chapter does not send
in its report, they are supposed to be and are counted as being in favor of the

project, whatever it may be.
^> One of the very few disagreeable events of the past year has been the breaking

up of the Alpha Chapter. Some time last October the Secretary of the Council
received a letter from Brother Boyd, of the Alpha, asking when he could see any
member of the Council in New York, and also asking us not to
reply to any letters
we might receive from the Alpha until we heard from him further. The Secretary
accordingly informed Brother Boyd of the time and place where the Secretary
\ could be seen. Nothing more was heard from the Chapter until Brother Boyd
", again wrote, telling us that the Alpha had voted to dissolve the
Chapter. Brother
; Boyd asked that the Council should transfer the archives over to him, and to
give
'^ him the power to re-establish the Chapter at the first favorable
opportunity. This
y the Council declined to do. The Council thereupon authorized the
Sigma Chapter
/ to send on a delegate to Harvard to investigate the trouble, and to take possession
\ of the archives in the name of the Executive Council. The Sigma failed to attend
to it. The Council then appointed Brother
Thompson a committee to go on to
Harvard and to report upon the condition of the
Alpha, and to take possession of
the archives of that Chapter. The report of this committee is below.
We are sorry to be obliged to call the attention of the Convention to an

apparent violation of the amendments to the Constitution
passed at the last
Canvention. The XiChapter reports having initiated two men as honorary
members. The Chapter can, we
hope, explain this to the satisfaction of the
Convention. The Phi Chapter
reports having expelled Mr. Rowley, a member of
that Chapter. We should recommend to the Convention that a
Chapter expelling
a member should
notify the Council and several Chapters, as at present, and that
the Council be directed to
report the matter to the Convention.
In view of the labor of
collecting the faxes from the several Chapters, the
Council would recommend some
legislation upon the subject.
The Council also suggest that the
subject of supplementary catalogues be
considered by the Convention.
The Council are very desirous that the
Chapters should be particular in sending
in their returns as soon as
possible. It is upon this return that they are taxed and
in case there is no late one the Council is

amount of money has been offered to the
Council if a
Chapter of the Fraternity

X5

should be established at Williams College. The Council accordingly suggest that

Report on the Alpha Chapt^.
To the Executive Council of the Psi Upsilon Fraternity.

Your committee appointed for an investigation into the matters of the Alpha
Chapter, respectfully reports :
That he has visited Harvard College and obtained information from all the
sources in his power, giving a hearing to all parties desiring it, and finds the fol
lowing facts :
I. That for a year past the Chapter has been in a failing condition, owing to a
lack of interest and enthusiasm on the part of some members.

II. That this lack of interest and enthusiasm has been caused by other society
connections 'on the part of its members. That there have been in the Chapter
rival factions 
the one of members of a sporting society called the Hasty Pudding,
and the other of a literary society called the Signet. That, in consequence of
complications with these societies, irreconcilable differences arose between the two
factions, which ultimately resulted in the vote to disband the Chapter. The

representatives of the Hasty Pudding, in the Chapter, claimed that no good men
could be found who would accept elections to Psi Upsilon, and that therefore the
Chapter should disband rather than to lower the standard of membership. They
charge that this extraordinary state of affairs was brought about by the ill-advised
and selfish course of Brother W. M. Boyd, who sought to make the Chapter sub

ordinate to the Signet, and who would sacrifice Psi Upsilon to the interest of the
latter Society. On the contrary, the representatives of the Signet, in the person of
Brother Boyd, charge Brother Fred. G. Fincke with having wickedly and traitor

ously sought the destruction of the Chapter, when it appeared that men of low,
convivial tastes and dissipated habits could not be introduced into its membership.

III. Your committee further finds that there
.
are no men at the present time
who are willimto assume control of the Chapter, but that there is good prospect
that there will soon be an
opportunity to resuscitate the Chapter on a sound
foundation.

i6

From the facts presented above, your committee has arrived at the following
conclusions ;

I. That whatever may have been the motives of the members of the Chapter
who proposed and carried forward the plan of dissolution, their action was wholly

unnecessai-y and inexpedient. That no state of affairs has at any time existed
which would warrant the of such a step as the dissolution of the
contemplation
Chapter.
II. That the Chapter should be considered not as dissolved and abandoned,
but merely as suspended, and that the Executive Council should be instructed to
re-establish it among the Psi Upsilons of the College and vicinity as soon as

practieable.
III. That an investigation should be ordered into the conduct of W. M. Boyd
and Fred. G. Fincke, with a view to
ascertaining upon whom rests the blame of
this unfortunate and inexcusable condition of affairs ; and that upon such investi

gation action should be taken in such a manner as may be constitutional and
expedient.
Respectfully submitted,
Daniel G. Thompson, Committee.
Cambridge, Mass., yune 2, 1873.

Chapters, all but fifteen copies of the Fraternity Catalogue of 1870, distributing

of the Psi
Upsilon Fraternity, that Article III. of the Constitution of the Fraternity be

Section 4. When a petition for the establishment of a

Upsilon Fraternity, that the Executive Council be sustained in their decision that
they had no power to allow any chapter to change its vote after

ported to them.

Chapter be instructed to inquire into the ad visa-

General Resolution No. 7. Resolved by the General Convention of the Psi

Upsilon Fraternity, that the Executive Council be instructed to report at the next
Convention a plan for preparing and issuing a revised edition of the Fraternity
Catalogue.
General Resolution No. 8. Resolved by the General Convention of the Psi
Upsilon Fraternity, that the Recorder of this and future Conventions be instructed
to forward the records and all other
Fraternity documents in his possession, to the
Executive Council as soon as possible after Convention.
General Resolution No. g. Resolved by the General Convention of the Psi

Upsilon Fraternity :
Seccion I. The Convention condemns in the strongest terms the action which
resulted in the abandonment of the Alpha Chapter, as unnecessary and unwarrant.
able, and hereby repudiates the action of said Chapter, and instructs the Executive
Council to cause its active progress to be resumed by taking such ineasures as

may be just and expedient.
Section 2. The members who voted for the dissolution of the Alpha Chapter
are hereby declared to have forfeited their right to membership in the Fraternity,
and are hereby suspended from the same until action can be taken upon them by
the Alpha Chapter, or by further decree of the Convention.
Section 3. The Executive Council is hereby requested to investigate in full
the conduct of Bros. W. M. Boyd and Fred G. Fincke in the premises, together
with that of such other members of said Alpha Chapter as they may deem neces
sary, and report to the Convention the result of such investigation.
Section 4. That the Executive Council be authorized to levy a tax often (io\
cents on each member of the Fraternity to defray expenses. 

General Resolution No. 10. Resolved by the General Convention of the Psi

Upsilon Fraternity, that the Chair be empowered to appoint a Committee to

whom shall be referred that portion of the unfinished business of the last Conven
tion entitled General Resolution No. 12.

General Resolution No. ii. Resolved by the General Convention of the Psi

Upsilon Fraternity, that the Treasurer of the Executive Council be instructed to
add interest at the rate of twenty per cent, to all Fraternity taxes remaining un

paid at the close of the Convention next succeeding the levy of said taxes.
General Resolution No. 12. Resolved by the General Convention of th Psi
Upsilon Fraternity, that the Executive Council be instructed to report all expul
sions at the Convention next following such expulsions.
We hereby certify that the foregoing General Resolutions were- duly passed at
the Fortieth Convention of the Psi Upsilon Fraternity.
Hanover, N. H., June 14, 1873.
